title: Norway Freezes Data Center Grid Reservations Until 2027 as Demand Tops National Peak, Turkey Signs Offshore Deals With Chevron and OMV, and Brent Crude Climbs Toward $96 on Gulf Strikes
subhead: Norwegian grid operator Statnett halts new power connections for data centers through August 2027, Turkey's TPAO partners with Chevron in Guinea-Bissau and signs a five-year pact with OMV, and Brent crude rebounds to $95.90 per barrel amid Gulf refinery and shipping attacks while NASA scales back its lunar nuclear reactor to 20 kilowatts.

sections.heading: Norway Pauses New Data Center Grid Reservations Until August 2027 as Requests Surpass Peak National Demand
sections.body:
Norway's state transmission system operator Statnett has suspended all new electricity grid capacity reservations for data centers until at least August 2027 after pending connection requests exceeded the country's entire peak power demand, OilPrice reports. The freeze was enacted alongside a new Norwegian government licensing framework designed to block energy-intensive cryptocurrency mining operations and prioritize grid capacity for domestic industrial decarbonization and defense manufacturing.

The European grid crunch is driving tech companies to seek dedicated power generation deals in Asia as well. According to Nikkei Asia and Channel NewsAsia, Japan's largest power generation company, JERA, has entered negotiations with Anthropic and Meta to co-develop dedicated power infrastructure for hyperscale AI data centers across Japan.
sections.whyItMatters: Even hydropower-rich Norway hitting a hard grid ceiling that forces a multi-year moratorium on data center connections demonstrates that physical electricity transmission—not chip supply—is becoming the primary bottleneck for AI expansion.

sections.heading: Turkey's TPAO Partners With Chevron on Guinea-Bissau Offshore Blocks and Signs Five-Year Pact With OMV
sections.body:
Turkish Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Alparslan Bayraktar announced that national oil company TPAO has signed a partnership agreement with US energy major Chevron to jointly explore and develop two offshore hydrocarbon blocks in Guinea-Bissau, Anadolu Agency reports. On the same day, TPAO signed a five-year Memorandum of Understanding with Austria's OMV and Romania's OMV Petrom covering joint upstream exploration, Black Sea gas cooperation, and regional energy trade, according to TRT World.

Speaking at the Energy Summit in Istanbul, Bayraktar also declared that 2027 will be the decision year for selecting international partners to build Turkey's planned second and third nuclear power plants in Sinop and Thrace (Tekirdağ) as the first reactor unit at Akkuyu nears commissioning. Meanwhile, 21 Turkish energy firms formed the largest foreign national delegation at the LIBYES 2026 Libya Energy Exhibition in Tripoli, even as OilPrice warned that political fallout from Ukraine's naval drone strike in Benghazi could complicate Tripoli's campaign to attract $20 billion in foreign oil investment.
sections.whyItMatters: Pairing a West African offshore venture with Chevron and a Black Sea/Danube framework with OMV expands TPAO from a domestic operator into an international upstream partner while Ankara prepares final partner selection for two new nuclear stations in 2027.

sections.heading: Brent Crude Rebounds Toward $96 on Gulf Attacks as Fulcrum LNG Warns High US Gas Prices Threaten Export Edge
sections.body:
Brent crude for January delivery climbed 1.3% to $95.90 per barrel on Thursday — up more than $6 from Monday's close of $89.37 — as drone and mine attacks across the Persian Gulf and Red Sea outweighed earlier projections of a global supply surplus, OilPrice and Standard Chartered report. Market jitters intensified after the Saudi-led Arab Coalition confirmed a Houthi attack targeting the Jazan oil refinery in southwestern Saudi Arabia, an explosion rocked Thailand's Bangchak oil refinery in Bangkok, and a deadly drone strike hit a military site in Kuwait.

In a Thanksgiving call to US troops in the Gulf, President Donald Trump asserted that the United States holds 'close to 50%' of world oil and does not need Middle Eastern crude, urging Tehran to reach a deal, Al Jazeera and Anadolu Agency report. However, inside the US gas sector, Fulcrum LNG warned that rising domestic Henry Hub natural gas prices driven by winter demand and AI power generation risk making US LNG exports uncompetitive in price-sensitive Asian markets, according to EnergyNow.
sections.whyItMatters: Brent's rapid $6 bounce back toward $96 shows how quickly physical strikes on Gulf refineries erase paper surplus forecasts, while rising domestic US power demand threatens the cheap feedstock advantage that fueled America's LNG export boom.

sections.heading: NASA Scales Back Lunar Nuclear Reactor From 100 kW to 20 kW as Cyberattack Shuts Down Wyoming Uranium Plant
sections.body:
NASA has quietly scaled back the target power output of its planned fission surface power reactor on the Moon from 100 kilowatts to 20 kilowatts due to mass, radiator cooling, and budget constraints ahead of its 2030 deployment goal, OilPrice reports. US space officials had previously framed the 100 kW reactor as essential to beating China and Russia to a permanent lunar base and establishing a safety 'keep-out zone' at the lunar south pole.

On Earth, nuclear fuel supply chains suffered a new disruption after Peninsula Energy shut down its Lance in-situ recovery uranium operation in Wyoming following a cyberattack that compromised plant and wellfield process control systems, leaving no confirmed restart date, according to The Register.
sections.whyItMatters: Cutting NASA's lunar reactor capacity by 80% reduces the power available for future lunar ice-mining and habitat operations, while the cyber shutdown of a live US uranium wellfield highlights operational-technology vulnerabilities across domestic nuclear fuel production.

sections.heading: Diesel Tanker Carrying 7,000 Tonnes Capsizes Off Ibiza Killing One as US Thanksgiving Storm Cuts Power to 960,000 Homes
sections.body:
The Maltese-flagged chemical and product tanker Med Emre, carrying up to 7,000 tonnes (1.2 million liters) of diesel fuel, capsized and sank approximately 46 kilometers off the Spanish island of Ibiza on Thursday, killing one crew member while Spanish maritime rescue teams pulled 17 sailors to safety and activated an emergency marine pollution containment plan, Reuters and the BBC report.

Across North America, a severe dual-coast Thanksgiving storm system knocked out electricity to more than 960,000 homes and businesses, triggered coastal flooding warnings, and forced the cancellation or delay of more than 2,300 flights, according to Business Insider, BBC, and TRT World. Meanwhile in Eastern Europe, repeated Russian missile and drone strikes left large districts of Kyiv facing prolonged daily electricity and heating blackouts as freezing temperatures set in, Al Jazeera reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Simultaneous grid blackouts affecting nearly a million US customers from winter storms and millions of Ukrainians from Russian strikes underscore the fragility of aging electrical distribution networks under extreme weather and wartime targeting.

bottomLine: Norway's freeze on new data center grid reservations until August 2027 and JERA's power talks with Anthropic and Meta in Japan highlight the intensifying global scramble for baseload electricity to run AI infrastructure. In traditional hydrocarbons and nuclear power, Brent crude's rebound toward $96 on Gulf refinery attacks, Turkey's new offshore partnerships with Chevron and OMV, and a cyberattack that shut down a Wyoming uranium plant show how geopolitical and cyber risks are tightening physical energy supply chains.
sources: OilPrice, EnergyNow, Anadolu Agency, TRT World, BBC, Reuters, Al Jazeera, The Register, Channel NewsAsia, Nikkei Asia, Business Insider
